facts.claim: Death registration in Surat Municipal Corporation is done through the Government of Gujarat's eOlakh Application since April 1, 2020.
facts.subject: death_registration
facts.evidence: Surat Municipal Corporation is using Government of Gujarat's eOlakh Application ( https://eolakh.gujarat.gov.in/ ) for death registration from 01/04/2020, hence online death certificate for death registered on or after this date will not be available.

facts.claim: Online death certificates for deaths registered on or after April 1, 2020, are not available through Surat Municipal Corporation's online services.
facts.subject: death_certificate
facts.evidence: hence online death certificate for death registered on or after this date will not be available.

facts.claim: A citizen pays Rs. 20 for an additional copy of a death certificate, which includes a Rs. 5 certificate fee and Rs. 15 administration charges.
facts.subject: death_certificate
facts.evidence: On payment of Rs. 20/- (Birth or Death certificate fee Rs. 5/- and administration charges Rs. 15/- = Rs. 20/-), a copy of birth & death certificate is available in Gujarati and English.

facts.claim: The nominee must submit a Death Registration Certificate and additional documents like FIR, Post Mortem Report, Police Inquest Report, and Police Conclusion Report or Final Report for processing.
facts.subject: death_certificate
facts.evidence: Step 1: The nominee submits an application along with the Death Registration Certificate and additional documents, including the FIR, Post Mortem Report, Police Inquest Report, and Police Conclusion Report or Final Report.

facts.claim: To get Indian citizenship for a child born to Indian parents in a foreign country, the child's birth must be registered at the nearest Indian Embassy/Consulate.
facts.subject: indian_citizenship_child
facts.evidence: In order to get Indian citizenship for a child born to Indian parent(s) in a foreign country, the birth of the child is to be registered at the nearest Indian Embassy/Consulate and thereafter (or at the same time) the parents can apply for issue of an Indian passport for the child.

facts.claim: Indian Missions/Posts can attest a birth certificate issued by Indian authorities if it is first authenticated by the Home Department of the concerned State/Union Territory and then by the Attestation Section of the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) in New Delhi or the MEA Branch Secretariats in Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Guwahati.
facts.subject: birth_certificate_attestation
facts.evidence: Yes, provided the birth certificate issued by the competent authorities has been authenticated by the Home Department of the concerned State/Union Territory in India and then by the Attestation Section of the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), New Delhi or the MEA Branch Secretariats in Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Guwahati.
